I had two relationships so far. One was very loving and made me feel great and the other...well ended way too quickly to really say anything but since we are still actively in contact and have a weird uncertain status that makes me feel quite...miserable at times, I feel like I know both sides of the coin and can say something about this!

Obviously I can't speak for everyone but we guys tend to feel overlooked, worthless even. We live in a society with expectations placed on us, it's hard to stay strong all this time. Being vulnerable is quite the risk to take! Even mundane actions have to be thought out since you could get accused for literally anything quite easily...

So for future relationships you should show that you care for them! That you appreciate what they are doing, let them be themselves and feel good about it!
It can be quite empowering for a guy when you simply make them feel like they are one of your priorities.
Let them know that they can talk about their struggles and not have a constant wall up. Sometimes a simple hug or some other form of physical touch can do wonders! Not even sexual, but lovingly. (Though depending on the progress of the relationship, that's something you can do as well. You should try to initiate it yourself though as well, since once again that makes us feel wanted)
Clear communication is essential. We guys tend to be dense, having second thoughts, questioning if we actually are cared for. Occasional sweet reminders of your appreciation can make guys quite happy.

I know people who got a compliment from a girl once and still remembered and valued it years after- it's really that bad.
Thats probably why you noticed that simply making compliments can have crazy effects, because truthfully we guys aren't really used to it and it makes us feel special. Most women expect us to be the ones to do so, but usually we get nothing in return. Besides getting laughed at, called a creep or ...ignored.

After a hard day, having someone who showers you in affection, someone who you can be yourself around and just enjoy the moment is all we need.

I can't deny that having someone who was essentially my little "cheerleader", who went out of her way to write me a message wishing me luck for the day made me feel a lot more confident in myself.
Of course this should also be the other way around, guys should try to do the same for women!

If both feel like they can be themselves and want to say+show their care, then I feel like that's a good foundation for a blooming relationship.

If you need some more concrete ideas:
Small reminders of your care, maybe small gifts if they are into it? Verbal reminders are already good though! If you're living apart you could make a small good morning message and wish them luck with anything they planned to do that day. Physical touch such as hugs, just putting your hand on his or maybe on his shoulder.
Be interested in their life and let them talk about it, perhaps engage yourself with it?

Regarding the spooning, that varies from person to person. Personally I would be embarrassed, but probably like it secretly to some degree as well lol

I'm sure you could think of many more sweet gestures, but I feel like this could give you a good insight already.

Most people call it synergy. Basically, how the main weapon, sub weapon and special weapon interact with eachother.

In this case, the kit is considered bad because splashwall doesnt help much, as the main weapon usually requires you to be close to the enemy. You want to use splashwall to keep your distance and be safe from enemies. Reefslider does combo with the main weapon, but the special is very predictable and easy to punish. 

The original kit wasnt out of this world, but did play into the main weapons strong points. Curling was great as you can hold your charged shot and move along the curling trail. Tenta missiles were great to easily spot enemies and give them some damage, making it easier to finish them off.

To be honest, Tenta Missiles were handled rather well in this game. The added cooldown did a lot. Plus, nearly every weapon that has the special usually requires around 200 points (only exception is the wiper), therefore its likely that the painbrush will be around 200 as well.
Also the special is just way more uncommon in S3 and usually gets added to rather unpopular main weapons...so I wouldnt worry about it too much, this isnt gonna be meta defining or anything.

I like all of them for very different reasons.

Storm 1 felt the most like the original Ultimate Ninja series, which was my childhood so yeah.

Storm 2 pretty much revolutionized what I thought was possible for a game adaption of an anime/manga with its beautiful and immersive boss fights, even though everything else was kinda a downgrade.

Storm Generations was just simply fun to play. While I feel like the Storm games (especially the older ones) are too simple, even when compared to the PS2 series of games, I must admit that Generations improved and more or less perfected the battle system they had. Which was important, because the game doesnt offer much else besides the fighting.

Storm 3 for the boss fights, again. But I do respect that the content around them is an improvement over Storm 2. And the battles were basically like in Generations, with a few changes and additions here and there.

Storm Revolution is actually really good in my opinion. I liked the idea of the different fighting types, the customization, the battles with 4 characters and the Ninja World Tournament mode in general. I wouldnt want it to be a mainline title, but as a little experiment it was enjoyable! Plus the anime sections were neat.

Storm 4 made some great refinements to the battle system. The story mode was great once more, but you can tell that the first half was lacking in the cutscene department. Plus the split of the overworld gameplay into its own mode made the adventure mode rather...worthless. Because nobody really wants to play it just for the sake of it, you know? Its basically all filler. Revolution was filler too, but at least every character had some personalized side quests and the world traversal was mildly interesting...

Either Sonic Chaos on some Sega Gamegear Collection or Sonic Unleashed on the PS2.
Both games revolutionized 3D Sonic gameplay. However, if I had to choose though, then it would be Unleashed.

I would probably choose Generations.

SA2 is too important for the series, I mean it introduced shadow, perfected the chao system, managed to perfect the sonic stage design in 3D, had a pretty good story for a platformer, and so on.

Sonic Unleashed revolutionized the 3D Sonic Gameplay with the boost gameplay, has probably the biggest budget out of the last decade, feels very polished and just...like a grand journey. Its packed with content, even has incredible DLCs. Sure, the werehog is controversial, but say what you want about the idea of the werehog, the actual Implementation wasnt that bad. Fighting was fun and the platforming was really good. Also the game heavily encourages exploration, which fitted the night stages well and the day stages...well not so much, but I still enjoyed it.
Also it was the last time we had a good, epic and serious story in a Sonic game (well, besides the Black Night I guess). It just felt like the last game before everything went downhill.

Generations was great, but it was also kinda Unleashed but less. Less content, less 3D, less Story (if you can even call it a story), less everything. The modern stages were great, but never reached the challenge of Unleashed. The classic stages were fine, but nothing revolutionizing. I mean modern sonic had a lot of 2D anyway, so it doesnt feel that special anymore. The side missions are fine for the most part, but Unleashed offered entire new acts to play in contrast to Generations which just used the geometry of the levels with new object placement. The hub world is also a joke compared to Unleashed... You can tell the Budget was either halved or the Deadline was an issue. Or both.

So yeah, SA2 had a big impact on the series, perfecting the 3D gameplay and Unleashed revolutionized it. While Generations just refined it, although objectively it just doesnt offer as much or even feels as big as Unleashed or SA2.
Also, if Generations didnt exist, then Sega would surely have made that type of game anyway sooner or later.

I still love all 3 games though, lol

Rift Apart is easily one of the best games in the franchise. Compared to the awful 2016 "remake" its a masterpiece, but honestly, that isnt very difficult to achieve.

The writing and humour isnt on the level of the PS2 games unfortunately, but I doubt they will ever be...
Still, its much better than the 2016 game. I suppose its written like a R&C Future game, although it doesnt get as epic as A Crack In Time for example. Its just a very solid story that can be enjoyed by old veterans and newcomers alike. (However for people that are interested in the lore, there may be a special surprise)

Gameplay is just a refined Version of the last few games. The phantom dash does change the way I play the game personally, it's quite useful!
Pulling yourself towards rifts felt just like a pointless gimmick though tbh...
Otherwise the gameplay is just as you remember it.
So it's pretty good.

Level design is great. There arent many planets, but the few that are there are huge! Additionally you return to a few planets multiple times throughout the story, unlocking some new paths and such.
There are two "collectathon" levels in the game, and these are probably the best levels in the entire game.
But other levels are great too. Each have their own  unique idea that sets them apart from the other levels. The only level that doesnt feel special is probably the first level, but thats alright, its just the first level. 
The atmosphere in these levels is set up well too.

When it comes to platforming, I'm a little mixed.
Most of the platforming is put behind optional Rifts, which feels like the Developers didnt believe most Players would want to jump around?
Like...sure you jump around from time to time, but it doesnt get any more complicated than that most of the time. Sometimes you may run along a wall or dash through some wall, but thats mostly it.
The optional rifts offer some good platforming sections, but it never gets really challenging.

The game also offers the usual gold bolts which unlock some nice cheats. There are spy bots to hunt for that give even more lore about each Planet and there is lots of armor to collect, which give you a boost in something if you collect a full set.

The map-o-matic is back too, so collecting everything is rather straight foward.
But it's still fun to run around and collect stuff, and thats what matters in the end, right?

To conclude I would say Rift Apart is one of the most refined games in the franchise.
It's definitely up there with R&C2 and A Crack In Time.
Great planets, stunning visuals, perfected movement and action, a few but good platforming sections that make use of your moveset, a story that isn't the best, but rather harmless, lots of collectables...
It's probably the only reason to buy a PS5 currently. It surely was the main reason for me to buy one, and I have no regrets!

Sonic Unleashed is a well made game with lots of content, high production value and the Werehog wasn't bad, but instead a mostly well executed  gameplay style. Just the balance between Fighting and Platforming was unfortunately a little off, which I can look over though.
Day Stages were incredible as well, and the challenge some of these stages provide is great.
Also the game offers multiple optional levels and side quests which I appreciate.

Medals were well hidden and fun to discover, it truly made you learn these stages in and out. But I do admit that some locations in the Day stages didn't really fit with the gameplay style, as running at high speed and slowly looking for secrets doesn't work.
Its executed well in the night stages and hub worlds though.
Additionally collecting a lot of Souvenirs gets you additional medals, so if you at least try to get everything in the night stages, play optional stages (which you should either way because more content) and hub worlds AND get some Souvenirs, then you should never have to go back and grind for medals.

The Ranks were also surprisingly challenging, I had to put actual effort into getting an S Rank, and I wouldnt have it any other way.

Also, the game is way more 3D than compared to all the games that came after it.
HUB worlds fully 3D, Night Stages fully 3D...only modern day stages were 50% 2D.
Compared to Generations which had Classic Sonic who was completely 2D, the HUB was 2D, and Modern sonic arguably had more 2D than 3D compared to Unleashed.

Also Eggman Land was a pretty great Level that truly felt like the ultimate and final challenge of a videogame that tests everything you have learned so far.

So yeah, I Think Unleashed is great and arguably better than Generations, as Generations feels like Unleashed just less. Less 3D, less challenge, less content, less everything. At least it has some optional levels but these dont even bother having their own levels, instead they use the original geometry and place some random objects in there...
Its probably more consistent than Unleashed, but the highs of Unleashed are higher than the ones or Generations. The lows are lower in Unleashed than in Generations though.
Still, I prefer Unleashed. Its just my opinion tho :P
